st: Whisk [[2 cup]] sorghum flour, [[1 cup]] all-purpose flour, [[0.5 tsp]] yeast and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Pour in [[3 cup]] warm water and whisk until the batter is smooth and runny, like thin pancake batter.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 8 hours or overnight, until bubbly and pleasantly sour.
Stir the batter. If it feels thick, whisk in a splash of water.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium heat and wipe with a little of the [[2 tbsp]] oil.
Pour in a small ladle of batter and tilt the pan so it spreads very thin, about 8 inches wide.
Cook for 2 minutes until the top is dry and the edges lift. Flip and cook 30 seconds more.
Stack the finished kisra on a plate under a cloth to keep warm. Serve with stews like mulah.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a small pan. Cook the okra for 5 minutes, then add the tomato, [[0.25 tsp]] salt and a splash of water. Simmer 8 minutes.
In a heavy pot, bring [[3 cup]] water and [[0.25 tsp]] salt to a boil.
Mix [[2 cup]] sorghum flour with the remaining [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until smooth with no lumps.
Pour the paste into the boiling water while stirring hard with a wooden spoon. Lower the heat.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring and pressing out any lumps, until the porridge is thick and pulls away from the pot.
Scoop the asida into a wet bowl and turn it into a smooth dome.
Make a dip in the middle and pour in the melted [[3 tbsp]] butter.
Serve with the okra sauce and [[0.5 cup]] yogurt on the side. Tear off pieces and use them to scoop.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 7 minutes until golden.
Add the beef and brown on all sides for 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Pour in [[3 cup]] water. Cover and simmer on low for 60 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Whisk [[0.25 cup]] peanut butter with a ladle of hot broth in a bowl until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Add the okra and simmer for 15 minutes until the stew is thick and the okra is tender.
Taste, adjust salt, and serve with kisra or asida.

ing: to taste, fish is already salty
st: Soak the dried fish in water for at least 4 hours, changing the water twice, to remove excess salt.
Drain the fish, remove bones and skin, and break the flesh into bite-size pieces.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 7 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes until they form a thick sauce.
Stir in [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and the fish with [[2 cup]] water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Mix [[3 tbsp]] peanut butter with a ladle of hot liquid until smooth and stir it in.
Simmer 10 more minutes until rich and thick. Taste and add salt only if needed. Serve with asida or rice.
Soak the fava beans in plenty of water overnight, at least 8 hours, then drain.
Put the beans in a pot with [[6 cup]] fresh water. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 90 minutes until very soft.
Drain, keeping a cup of the cooking liquid.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the onion for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and [[1 tsp]] cumin for 1 minute.
Add the beans, tomato and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 8 minutes, mashing about half of the beans with a fork, adding liquid if dry.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice.
Spoon into bowls, drizzle with the remaining [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] parsley, and serve with bread.
Bring [[2.5 cup]] water and [[0.25 tsp]] salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Mix [[2 cup]] millet flour with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] cold water into a smooth paste.
Slowly stir the paste into the boiling water, stirring hard so no lumps form.
Lower the heat and cook for 12 minutes, stirring often, until a thick dough pulls from the sides.
Wet your hands and shape the dough into small balls about the size of a lime.
Place the balls in bowls and pour over the warm milk.
Drizzle with [[3 tbsp]] melted butter and sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] sugar. Serve warm.
